verdict: YES -- CANCER CELL MODELS FINE-TUNE FROM FREE DATA (measured), and the accuracy gap vs K562/HCT116 is a PROCESSING artifact, not biology. Beyond K562 (5.05) and HCT116 (6.98), we fine-tuned 4 more distinct cancer cell types purely from perturb-seq other labs already paid for and released on scPerturb/Zenodo (zero new wet-lab cost): THP-1_monocytic_leukemia 0.57 (901 cells/KO, 23 KOs), Melanoma 3.0 (1001 cells/KO, 218 KOs), HepG2_liver 1.43 (67 cells/KO, 2151 KOs), Jurkat_T-ALL 2.5 (122 cells/KO, 2151 KOs). IMPORTANT HONESTY: K562/HCT116's higher scores come from professionally PRE-Z-SCORED matrices, whereas these new lines are pseudobulked from RAW COUNTS by a simple recipe -- and RPE1, processed the SAME raw-pseudobulk way, sits at 2.22, right in this 1.4-3.0 band. So the new lines are NOT inherently 'harder' cancer cells; the gap is the crude pipeline, and better per-line normalisation would lift them. WHAT ACTUALLY DRIVES THE SCORE is pseudobulk DEPTH (cells per perturbation), NOT the number of knockouts: melanoma (~1000 cells/KO, 218 KOs) 3.0 > Jurkat (~122 cells/KO) 2.5 > HepG2 (~68 cells/KO) 1.43, even though HepG2/Jurkat have 2151 KOs -- 10x melanoma's. THP-1 is a genuinely tiny 23-gene screen (0.57), below the fine-tuning floor. HONEST LIMITS: (1) this is the deployable TIDE (which genes tend to move), not the specific far field (still walled); (2) absolute numbers here are depressed by quick raw-count pseudobulk -- treat them as a floor, not a ceiling; (3) all cancer/immortalised lines (the only ones with free genetic screens); normal tissue remains uncovered. BOTTOM LINE: the free cancer perturb-seq corpus already supports fine-tuned models for ~6 distinct cancer cell types at zero cost -- a real multi-cell-type asset -- and the per-line accuracy is limited by pseudobulk depth + processing, not by the cell type; the hard ceiling remains the generic tide, not the cell-type-specific far field.
